blocks.text: This video shows how to draw an icon in Pixodesk SVG Editor, from a few simple shapes, and use it on a web page as an ordinary image. Let's start with the background, a square tile.

blocks.alt: A rectangle, nearly as big as the canvas.

blocks.text: A rectangle, nearly as big as the canvas. Icons look friendlier with soft corners, so let's round them.

blocks.alt: One corner radius rounds all four corners.

blocks.text: One corner radius rounds all four corners. Then, let's paint it sky blue.

blocks.alt: Its fill colour is now sky blue.

blocks.text: Its fill colour is now sky blue. Next, the sun, an orange circle in the top corner.

blocks.alt: Holding Shift while drawing keeps it a perfect circle.

blocks.text: Holding Shift while drawing keeps it a perfect circle. The cloud is built from simple shapes. Three white circles, and a rectangle for a flat bottom.

blocks.alt: Four overlapping shapes, in the outline of a cloud.

blocks.text: Four overlapping shapes, in the outline of a cloud. Let's select all four, and unite them into one shape.

blocks.alt: Unite merges them into a single path, the cloud.

blocks.text: Unite merges them into a single path, the cloud. A soft gradient gives it some depth.

blocks.alt: A linear gradient, from white to light blue.

blocks.text: A linear gradient, from white to light blue. The icon is ready. Let's save it as SVG, into the web project.

blocks.alt: A heading, and the icon file, already next to the page.

blocks.text: A heading, and the icon file, already next to the page. Let's add the icon as an ordinary image.

blocks.alt: An image tag, pointing at the SVG file. A still icon needs nothing more.

blocks.text: An image tag, pointing at the SVG file. A still icon needs nothing more. Let's open the page.

blocks.alt: There it is. It stays sharp at any size, because it is vector.

blocks.text: There it is. It stays sharp at any size, because it is vector. So, a few simple shapes, united and coloured, saved as a clean SVG file, and used like any other image.
